mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 6.0% for three consecutive months indicates weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer demand and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
